home.title: Support research at the University of Turin – ideaBlume
home.h1: Support research at the University of Turin
home.intro: ideaBlume is the crowdfunding site for research projects at the University of Turin: choose a project, donate even a few euros and follow the results. The site is run by the University's ideaBlume Office. {link:chi-siamo.html|About us and how we work}
home.how_title: How it works, in three steps

how.d: Each project tells you who proposes it, what the money is for and how far it is from its goal.
From {min} upwards, with a reward or as a free donation. No need to register.

how.t: If the goal is reached, the University matches it
how.d: This applies to projects in the University programme. If the goal is not reached, we return your donation: this is the all-or-nothing rule.

home.promo_title: Do you have a research project or want to work with the University?
home.promo_text: Researchers at the University of Turin can apply to the University programme with a project. Associations, schools and local organisations can propose a partnership with a research group.

programma.title: University programme – ideaBlume
programma.intro: In one sentence: every year the University of Turin selects some projects from its research groups, supports them during the campaign and, if they reach their goal, adds an amount equal to the goal, up to {tetto} per project. {DV}
programma.inspired: The programme described here is simulated and inspired by real university crowdfunding initiatives.
programma.status_now: {anno} edition: phase 4 of 4, campaigns running until {data}.
programma.status_next: Applications for the {anno_prossimo} edition: opening and closing dates {DV}

phases.d: Sessions to learn how to present the project and run a campaign.
A University committee chooses projects based on quality, impact and feasibility.
The ideaBlume Office helps groups prepare their page, rewards and budget.
Campaigns last {dmin} to {dmax} days. When the goal is reached the University adds the same amount.

match: The match applies only if donations reach the goal by the end date.
The University adds an amount equal to the goal, up to {tetto} per project. {DV}
Donations above the goal go to the project's second goal, if there is one, and are not matched. {DV}
If the goal is not reached, donations are returned and the University adds nothing (“all or nothing”).
programma.example: The “Healthy hives” project has a goal of €6,000. Supporters have donated €7,800: the goal is reached, so the University adds €6,000. The extra €1,800 goes to the second goal. In total the project receives €13,800.
programma.who: Research groups at the University of Turin led by a permanent staff member (professor or researcher). Research fellows and PhD students can be part of the group. {DV}
req: A use of funds explained item by item.
Results that the public can understand and a plan to share them with supporters.
Simple rewards that the group can really deliver.
programma.how: Fill in the {link:candidatura.html|application form} before the call closes. Dates for the {anno_prossimo} edition: {DV}
programma.editions_caption: Programme projects by year (calculated from project data)
programma.e_note: For the current year the numbers change until the campaigns close; the co-funding shown is the amount expected for projects that have already reached their goal.

come.title: How it works – ideaBlume
come.intro: ideaBlume collects donations for research projects at the University of Turin. Here are the steps for donors, for people proposing a project and for groups with an ongoing campaign.
toc: For groups with an ongoing campaign

donor.d: Look at the topic, the group, the use of funds and the status of the campaign.

donor.t: Choose a reward or a free donation
donor.d: Free donations start at {min}. Rewards are small thank-you gifts from the group.

donor.t: Enter your details and choose whether to show your name
donor.d: No need to register. You can donate anonymously.
By card, PayPal, Satispay or bank transfer. Before confirming you see the total including the fee.

donor.t: When the campaign ends we tell you the result
donor.d: Goal reached: the money goes to the group and, for programme projects, the University matches it. Goal not reached: we return your donation.

promoter.d: Research groups at the University of Turin; associations, schools and organisations can partner with a group.

promoter.t: Read the programme requirements and deadlines
promoter.d: Goal, use of funds, rewards and call dates.
A form of about 10 minutes. Your data stays saved while you fill it in.

promoter.t: Take part in training and selection
promoter.d: The ideaBlume Office will contact you with the dates.

promoter.t: Prepare your page with the Office
promoter.d: Texts in Italian and English, rewards, budget.
Publish updates and, at the end, a report with the spending.

come.groups_title: For groups with an ongoing campaign
groups: Updates: send text and photos to the Office ({email_programma}); we publish them within 2 working days. {DV}
Content in two languages: write each text once in Italian and once in English, in two separate fields: the site shows one language at a time. Title up to 80 characters, subtitle up to 160.
Goal exceeded: ask the Office to add a second goal with an amount and a purpose: it will appear in the box next to “Support”.
A problem with the site? {link:contatti.html#scrivici|Report it with the contact form}, choosing “Problem with the site”.
come.doubts: Read the {link:faq.html|FAQ} or the {link:glossario.html|glossary}, or {link:contatti.html|contact us}.

costi.title: How much it costs
costi.donor: For donors: ideaBlume adds no extra cost to your donation. The payment provider charges a fee (for example 1.8% + €0.35 by card, PayPal or Satispay), shown before you confirm. {DV}
costi.promoter: For groups selected by the programme: any publication fee and included services {DV}. This prototype shows no amounts because the sources do not report them.
costi.partner: For associations and external organisations: proposing a partnership is free and does not commit your organisation.

proponi.title: Propose a project – ideaBlume
proponi.intro: There are two ways to bring a project to ideaBlume: apply to the University programme, if you are part of a research group at the University of Turin, or propose a partnership, if you represent an association, a school or another organisation.
proponi.res_title: Do you do research at the University of Turin?
proponi.res_text: You can apply to the co-funding programme with your group's project. You need a financial goal, a clear use of funds and a permanent staff member as principal investigator.
proponi.ext_title: Do you represent an association, a school or an organisation?
proponi.ext_text: You cannot launch a campaign on your own, but you can propose an idea to carry out with a research group: the ideaBlume Office looks for the right group and puts you in touch. {DV}
time: Applications to the programme: once a year, dates {DV}
Reply to a partnership proposal: within 10 working days, by phone or email. {DV}
proponi.examples_title: Examples of projects with the local community
proponi.examples: The project {link:progetto-scienza-doposcuola.html|“Science workshops in neighbourhood after-school clubs”} was started by associations in Barriera di Milano and Falchera together with the Department of Philosophy and Education Sciences.
proponi.groups_link: Already running a campaign? Read the {link:come-funziona.html#gruppi|guidance for groups}.

chi.title: About us – ideaBlume
chi.intro: ideaBlume is the crowdfunding site for research projects at the University of Turin. It is run by the University's ideaBlume Office. {DV}
what: We publish only projects by research groups at the University of Turin.
We check each group's budget and rewards before publication.
We run the University co-funding programme.
We ask every group for a final report with the spending, published on the project page.
chi.money: If the goal is reached, the money goes to the group's department, earmarked for the project. If not, it goes back to the donors. {DV}
chi.prototype: ideaBlume is a prototype created by students of the Human-Computer Interaction course at the University of Turin. Projects, people, contacts and amounts are fictional; information still to be confirmed is marked with {DV}.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions – ideaBlume
faq.count_0: No questions match. Try another word or {link:contatti.html|write to us}.
faq.not_found: Call us on {tel_link} ({orari}) or write to {email_aiuto_link}. We reply within {giorni} working days.

q.q: Can I donate without choosing a reward?
a: Yes. Choose “Free donation” and enter the amount, from {min} upwards.
Rewards are just a thank-you: they are not required.

q.q: What is the minimum amount?
a: {min} for a free donation, for every project.
For a reward, the minimum is the price shown next to it.

q.q: Do I need to register to donate?
a: No. We only need your name, surname and email for the confirmation.

q.q: How can I pay and how much does it cost?
a: You can pay by: {metodi}.
The payment provider charges a fee, which you see in the summary before confirming (for example 1.8% + €0.35 by card, PayPal or Satispay). There is no fee from us for bank transfers. {DV}

q.q: My payment did not go through: what should I do?
a: Nothing has been charged. You can try again straight away: the details you entered stay saved.
Try another payment method, for example a bank transfer.
If the problem continues, call us on {tel_link} ({orari}): we will help you complete the donation.

q.q: What happens if the project does not reach its goal?
a: We return your donation: this is the all-or-nothing rule.
The refund goes back to the same payment method within 15 days of the end date. The payment fee may not be refunded. {DV}

q.q: The project has already reached its goal: is it still worth donating?
a: Yes, as long as the campaign is open. Extra donations go to the second goal shown in the project box.
Donations above the goal are not matched by the University. {DV}

q.q: How does the University match work?
a: If a programme project reaches its goal, the University adds an amount equal to the goal, up to {tetto}. {DV}
{link:programma.html#raddoppio|Read an example}.

q.q: Can I donate anonymously? Who sees my name?
a: Yes: in the form choose “Donate anonymously”. The public sees “Anonymous supporter”.
The research group still receives your name and email to thank you and send your reward. The amount is never public. {DV}

q.q: Will I get a receipt? Is the donation tax-deductible?
a: After donating you receive a confirmation email with a summary.
Tax receipt and tax relief: {DV}

q.q: When will I get my reward?
a: After the campaign closes, if the goal is reached. The group will write to ask for your address, if needed.

q.q: Who can propose a project?
a: Research groups at the University of Turin, with a permanent staff member as principal investigator. {DV}
{link:proponi.html|Read who can propose}.

q.q: We are an association or a school: can we take part?
a: Yes, as a partner of a research group: {link:collabora.html|propose a partnership}. The ideaBlume Office looks for the right group. {DV}
Sending the proposal does not commit you and is free.

q.q: When can we apply?
a: Once a year, through a call. Dates of the next edition: {DV}

q.q: How much does it cost to propose a project?
a: Proposing a partnership is free.
For groups selected by the programme, any publication and service costs: {DV}

q.q: How long does a campaign last?
a: {dmin} to {dmax} days.

q.q: How do we publish updates and the final report?
a: Send text and photos to the Office ({email_programma}): we publish them in the project's “Updates” section. {DV}
At the end we ask for a report with the spending, which we also send to supporters.

q.q: Do we have to write content in two languages?
a: Yes, in Italian and in English, in separate fields: the site shows one language at a time. {link:come-funziona.html#gruppi|Read the guidance}.

q.q: Who runs ideaBlume?
a: The University of Turin's ideaBlume Office. {DV} {link:chi-siamo.html|About us}.

q.q: How do I know the money really goes to research?
a: Every project publishes the use of funds item by item and, at the end, a report with the actual spending.
The money goes to the group's department, earmarked for the project. {DV}

q.q: How can I talk to a person?
a: Call us on {tel_link} ({orari}) or write to {email_aiuto_link}.

q.q: Is this a real site?
a: No: it is a teaching prototype. You cannot really donate and the projects are fictional.

glossario.title: Glossary – ideaBlume
glossario.intro: Crowdfunding words explained simply. On ideaBlume each concept always has the same name.

terms.d: Raising money online: many people donate small amounts to make a project happen.
The minimum amount the project must raise by the end date. If it is not reached, donations are returned.
The ideaBlume rule: the group receives the money only if the goal is reached by the end date. Otherwise we return your donation.
A higher amount, with a specific purpose, for projects that have already reached their goal. Donations above the goal go to it.
For programme projects: if the goal is reached, the University adds an amount equal to the goal, up to {tetto}.
The initiative through which the University selects some projects, supports them and co-funds them.
A small thank-you from the group for people who donate at least a certain amount, for example a postcard or a lab visit. It is not required.
A donation without a reward, of the amount you prefer, from {min} upwards.
Someone who donates to a project.
The University people who propose and carry out the project. The principal investigator leads the group.
The cost charged by the payment provider (card, PayPal, Satispay). You see it before confirming your donation.
The text in which the group describes the results and how it spent the money.
The year in which the campaign took place. For programme projects it is the programme edition.
